newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end shade weaker despite yen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end shade weaker despite yen.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei stock index futures ended a shade weaker on Monday with strong dollar/yen providing minimal supportive impact, dealers said.
Trade volume was thin ahead of a public holiday in Japan on Tuesday and the release of U.S. economic data.
The June Nikkei contract fluctuated within a narrow 160-point range but ended 35 points lower at 18,615. Volume was relatively low at 8,525 contracts overall.
Dealers said the dollar's strong posture after the weekend Group of Seven (G7) nations meeting was mainly shrugged off as a weak yen would only lend temporary support.
"A stronger U.S. dollar does not remove the fact the U.S. government will pressure Japan if the trade surplus becomes wider," a dealer with a U.S. investment house said.
The market was also sensitive to expectations for further fiscal tightening in the United States, which would widen the gap between U.S. and Japanese interest rates and prove volatile to stocks.
Dealers said the U.S. quarterly employment figures on Tuesday and non-farm payrolls on Friday, will be closely watched.
Meanwhile, the June Nikkei was seen as likely to break near-term support at 18,550, but hold above 18,300.
The Taiwan MSCI Arpil futures contract settled at 364.2 points, compared with a previous close at 365. Overall volume was a robust 4,304 contracts.
Turnover was spurred by late selling in the Taiwan cash market following six consecutive days of gains, and the expiry of the April contract on Tuesday.
Dealers said volume was dominated by clients rolling out of their positions, particulary in the nearby months.
